+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M73030WWZF8M6HM1S3XS0D60
+- 01M7303G0Q7Q2N9GHQ1T8YE77Q
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8380'
+title: 'MT-15: Test that a sandboxed registry starts no process'
+---
+## What
+The MT-15 requirement: a test makes a registry in `sandboxed` mode and confirms that no capability starts a process.
+
+New `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SandboxedRegistryNoProcessTests.swift`:
+- Make a `sandboxed` registry with every capability that `sandboxed` mode permits: `withFiles`, `withGit`, snapshots, `withEnvironment`, `withWeb` (with a stub search backend, no network), `withSessions` if a test double exists, and an `MCPServer` on an in-memory transport.
+- Record the child processes of the test process with `proc_listchildpids(getpid())` (libproc) before the build.
+- Build the registry, then run one `runCode` snippet that calls one read verb of each noun (for example `files.read`, `git.status`, `environment.get`).
+- Record the child processes again. The set of new child PIDs must be empty.
+- Also confirm that the noun list has no `shell` and that `MCPServerPool` has no `StdioServerProcess`.
+
+The test must not depend on the speed of the machine: no time limit, no sleep. Other tests can start processes in parallel, so compare only child PIDs whose parent is this process and that started after the first record. If parallel tests make the set unstable, put this suite in `.serialized` with the suites that start processes, or count `posix_spawn` calls through a test hook in `ProcessLedger.swift`, and say which in the commit.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The test exists and passes in `sandboxed` mode.
+- [ ] The test fails when a shell capability or a stdio server is forced into the registry (confirm this one time by a temporary change, then revert).
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SandboxedRegistryNoProcessTests.swift` as above.
+- [ ] Run `swift test` one time; all tests pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file

-- Make a `sandboxed` registry with every capability that `sandboxed` mode permits: `withFiles`, `withGit`, snapshots, `withEnvironment`, `withWeb` (with a stub search backend, no network), `withSessions` if a test double exists, and an `MCPServer` on an in-memory transport.

-- Record the child processes again. The set of new child PIDs must be empty.
-- Also confirm that the noun list has no `shell` and that `MCPServerPool` has no `StdioServerProcess`.
+Research: only two code paths in `Sources` start a child process: `ShellRunner` (`Subprocess.run`) and `StdioServerProcess` (`posix_spawn`). Each child is recorded in `ProcessRegistry.global` and in `ProcessLedger` (`Capabilities/ProcessLedger.swift`). `ProcessRegistry.global` is global, and other tests start processes in parallel, so a count of global children is not stable. Do NOT count PIDs and do NOT wait for a time.

-The test must not depend on the speed of the machine: no time limit, no sleep. Other tests can start processes in parallel, so compare only child PIDs whose parent is this process and that started after the first record. If parallel tests make the set unstable, put this suite in `.serialized` with the suites that start processes, or count `posix_spawn` calls through a test hook in `ProcessLedger.swift`, and say which in the commit.
+New `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SandboxedRegistryNoProcessTests.swift`, structural checks:
+- Make a `sandboxed` registry with every capability that `sandboxed` mode permits: `withFiles`, `withGit`, snapshots, `withEnvironment`, `withWeb` (with a stub search backend, no network), and an `MCPServer` on an in-memory transport.
+- Confirm that no registered capability is a `ShellCapability` and that the noun list has no `shell`.
+- Confirm that the `MCPServerPool` of the builder has no `StdioServerProcess`.
+- Add a per-registry spawn hook if necessary: an internal `spawnObserver` (a closure that `ShellRunner` and `StdioServerProcess` call before each spawn, given through the builder, default nil). Run one `runCode` snippet that calls one read verb of each noun (for example `files.read`, `git.status`, `environment.get`) and confirm that the observer of this registry got zero calls. The observer is per registry, thus parallel tests do not change the result.

 ## Acceptance Criteria
 - [ ] The test exists and passes in `sandboxed` mode.
 - [ ] The test fails when a shell capability or a stdio server is forced into the registry (confirm this one time by a temporary change, then revert).
+- [ ] The test has no time limit, no sleep and no global process count.

 ## Tests
 - [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsMultitoolTests/SandboxedRegistryNoProcessTests.swift` as above.
+- [ ] A test in `open` mode confirms that the observer gets one call for a `shell.execute` of `true`, so the hook is known to work.
 - [ ] Run `swift test` one time; all tests pass.

 ## Workflow
-- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #step1 #tests
